summary: Sumter County Forestry Commission lookout; the only source names it with county and agency, and none gives a build date or describes the site now.

evidence.supports: Listed as a Forestry Commission lookout in Sumter County
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Sumter County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: First commission tower erected in August 1930 near Camden
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: Most tower sites had ten acres, the tower and a year-round operator dwelling
evidence.quote: Most tower sites consisted of 10 acres of land, the tower, and a year-round dwelling for the operator.

evidence.supports: From the 1960s most operators were women, often married to firefighters
evidence.quote: From the 1960s on, most South Carolina tower operators were women; frequently their husbands were employed as firefighters.

evidence.supports: Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: Network eventually included more than 130 towers, used for 65 years
evidence.quote: The tower network eventually included more than 130 towers and was used for 65 years to detect wildfires.
The SCFC lookout tower system was decommissioned in 1994.

evidence.supports: More than 100 towers closed as the commission moved into a new era
evidence.quote: the Forestry Commission moved into a new era and more than 100 towers around the state closed
Today, only 30 of them remain standing.

evidence.supports: Some towers used for radio antennas and other communication equipment
evidence.quote: fire lookout towers are used here and there around the state for radio antennas and other communication equipment

sources.title: Looking out for last fire towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The commission's own history gives October 1, 1993 for closing its tower system; the Post and Courier gives 1994 for decommissioning. Both are kept as separate dates.

notes_for_editor: Only the lookout-history stub names this tower (name, county, agency). It gives no build date, height, staffing or status, so the story leaves those out. OpenStreetMap node 357114129 (tower:type observation, ele 40) carries no date or status tags and is not cited. A web search surfaced a Rosemary Fire Tower in Sumter County on former Manchester State Forest land; no source I read ties it to Black River, so it is not used. Worth a check of Sumter County history or SCFC records if a source turns up.
